label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Here's the post:

---

@Kavya, this is for you, and for everyone in our Foundry91 cohort who has been tagging me under your post.

I'll start with where I got it wrong. When we made offers to two engineers from SitterNest, I knew where they worked from day one. I should have called you before making those offers, not after. That's on me, and I'm sorry.

Since a few numbers are going around, here's what actually happened, plainly.

We put up a backend developer opening on the DabbaDost LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone. The first person applied on his own on 19 September. The second came about two weeks later, as a referral from the first. Nobody from my side DMed or approached anyone.

The offers were 22% over their current CTC. Not 40%. Both joined us on 3 November.

On ESOPs: we do have a pool. It's small, but it's real, and it has been on paper since January. We haven't promised anything we don't have.

I did message you after the second offer was accepted. That was late, and I understand why it landed the way it did.

And I want to say this in public too. You sat with me in our Koramangala office till 1am before demo day, fixing our Razorpay webhook mess. I haven't forgotten that and I won't. You've helped me a lot through this batch. This post isn't a fight. I'm writing it because I respect you, and I didn't want to leave this sitting in the comments.

The bigger issue is that this will happen again. There are 11 startups in our batch, and we all hire from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. Good people will move between our companies sometimes, and that's fine. Next time it could be me on the other side of it.

So here's a simple rule I'd like us to try in the cohort: if you're interviewing someone who works at another company in our batch, give that founder a heads-up before you make the offer. Before, not after. It doesn't take away anyone's freedom to change jobs. It just means no founder finds out from a resignation email.

Kavya, I'd really like to have a coffee or a call with you this week, or whenever you're okay with it. No agenda, just two people from the same batch talking. I'll listen first.

To the other founders in Foundry91 cohort 4: would you be up for the rule? Tell me what you'd change.

---

It's about 423 words and roughly 2,400 characters with spaces, so it fits both limits. Make sure you tag her properly on LinkedIn so the @ turns into a real mention. I left the two engineers unnamed, as you asked.
